Decision-feedback equalizers (DFEs) are integral to high-speed fiber-optic transmission systems for mitigating chromatic dispersion. We demonstrate the effectiveness and computational efficiency of our proposed nMAP implementation through comparisons with standard nMAP results, utilizing both numerical simulations and actual field-test datasets.

In this study, we analyze feeble lensing signals within the Pan-LC dataset, demonstrating that a modest aggregate of source-galaxy shear measurements can directly probe the average mass of SNIa host galaxies with substantial precision. Specifically, we develop a "smart" measurement approach that effectively filters out non-lensing sources of covariance, such as intrinsic variability and incomplete photometric corrections, to significantly enhance the robustness of the resulting statistics. Although this proposed "smart" method yields a larger effective variance in shear due to intrinsic covariance, simulations indicate it produces biased estimates of less than approximately 10% even for small sample sizes by correctly addressing intrinsic covariance. Applying this smart method to a sample of merely 100 SNIAs yields a 3.0% biased 1 estimated average shear of $\langle\gamma\rangle=0.003\pm0.001$ (1 estimated variance included), while utilizing the full Pan-LC dataset of 10,000 SNIAs refines this to a 1 estimated percentage of bias <1%, with a final estimated standard error.

MRI scanners are increasingly utilized to detect malignancies, with these tumours often appearing as distinct abnormal white masses in MRI imagery. This study evaluates various techniques designed for identifying tumours within MRI data. Traditional image processing approaches were initially employed to refine the MRI pictures for subsequent processing. Following this refinement, multiple classification algorithms were applied to distinguish between healthy tissue and tumours, with the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) method yielding the best performance with an 87.66% success rate. In contrast, Deep Learning (DL) architectures were also assessed to determine their efficacy in medical tumour detection. The implementation of two specific Deep Learning models—the VGG-19 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and the Dense-connected Fully Supervised Artificial Neural Network (Dense ANN)—revealed that VGG-19 achieved the superior accuracy of 94.16%. Consequently, by integrating traditional processing strategies with the VGG-19 model, a robust solution was established for identifying tumours in MRI scans.

We introduce a fresh framework for the degeneration of Bernoulli numbers and various associated degeneration operations within a commutative ring devoid of division, specifically within $\mathbb{Z}$. This approach is rooted in an innovative interpretation involving the operatorial inversion of formal differential equations. Such decomposition enables an explicit representation of these numbers in $\mathbb{Z}$ through rational coefficients. Furthermore, an innovation in integer matrix theory—specifically, the definition of an "integer matrix of unit determinant" (non-zero real eigenvalues all equal to 1)—yields a new result: an integer matrix of unit determinant can transform an integer matrix of unit determinant such that the real numbers (not necessarily 0) are preserved. Finally, an exploration into the relation between this method and an existing approach by Guo and Jiang has been initiated.

Stellar activity noise poses a significant challenge in determining the true exoplanet velocity signals via radial velocity methods. To mitigate this, a parametric model incorporating a Gaussian kernel was applied to select a reduced subset of spectral lines. The parameters of this kernel were optimized using a genetic algorithm to minimize both line count and noise correlation. Testing on an artificial dataset with a 10-day signal contaminated by 24-hour stellar variability indicated that this selection strategy reduced the RV noise standard deviation by 40%, although it slightly increased any bias. These artificial results were then validated using real observations of HD 162626 processed through least-squares deconvolution. The study further assessed the impact of line choice on this technique by comparing the parametric approach against a random line selection method. Results from the random selection demonstrated a noise standard deviation approximately 20% lower than that achieved by the parametric method, and artificial dataset analysis confirmed that the initial reduction in noise variability did not necessarily eliminate bias in the RV measurements.

We introduce two novel protocols designed for peer-to-peer creation of temporary gathering points in Wireless Sensor Networks. The first protocol, **Bidirectional Link Caliber Estimation (BLCE)**, determines the optimal bidirectional communication connections between a source and a destination. Addressing multihop scenarios, a second protocol, **Hierarchical Scoping Sectoring (HS²)**, organizes a tree-structured temporary gateway from source to destination. Collectively, these methods enable a range of multi-party applications, including data aggregation, in-wire computation, and collaborative image acquisition. Experimental outcomes indicate that BSCE and HS² enhance end-to-end communication overhead by a factor ranging from 3 to 13 compared to the well-known DATA-GATHER protocol.

We introduce a methodology for evaluating context-assisted object recognition across diverse scenarios. Our approach analyzes the interplay between context utilization and recognition accuracy by categorizing data according to the configuration of both object and scene context. Through large-scale annotation of 12 object categories and 12 categories of deceptive misclassifications, we trained and evaluated PPM and COV context-enhanced predictors alongside standard object detectors. Our findings reveal that 54% of data points possess at least one corresponding context cue, while misdegenere data accounts for 30%. Notably, 40% of misdegenerative samples provide zero context, and among those offering at least some context, 40% remain ambiguous with both positive and negative indicators present. Consequently, context-assisted recognizers achieve their highest F-scores at 81% for positive context and 50% for negative context, respectively, though they drop to just 21% on ambiguous data.

This research examines a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system defined on a smooth, bounded domain within $\mathbb{R}^2$ that includes singularity at the origin and follows Trudinger-Moser growth. The primary objective is to demonstrate the existence of ground state solutions by direct variational methods, employing a critical compactness argument within the Sobolev context.

The authors introduce and examine new upper limits for the tail probability of the sum of binary, zero-mean, and uniformly bounded random variables that exhibit a specific form of negative correlation, characterized by the property that the expectation of any variable, conditioned on all others, lies within the interval $[0,1]$. These findings are applied to the Carathéodory extension theorem and the analysis of the typical set in information theory. Specifically, a somewhat simpler, related bound derived herein effectively improves the exponential concentration inequality originally established by Peres.

This study examines the cos$\phi_R$-dependent component of the differential cross section for hadron pair emission in deeply inelastic scattering with longitudinally polarized proton targets, specifically analyzing the contribution from two sequential hadrons. We detail how this term arises from quark antiquark correlations within the proton structure and highlight its utility in investigating the internal dynamics of hadronization. Furthermore, we detail the influence of both intrinsic and relative transverse motions of constituent partons on this correlation term. Regarding the latter, we observe that while a non-zero mean value for the second hadron's transverse momentum is required to generate this correlation when the first hadron is unpolarized, the correlation persists even if the second hadron is spin-polarized. Additionally, we explore this effect using perturbative QCD in the di-hadron scattering process involving two transversely polarized protons within the framework of twist-3 factorized formalism. Our findings indicate that this correlation term is kinemematically suppressed at leading power in high power di-hadron scattering with double spin asymmetry in this specific scenario.

We enhance the existing Wikipedia-based entity recommendation system associated with the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph. By incorporating a layered node2vec technique to extract features from Wikipedia page interaction networks, we aim to significantly improve recommendation accuracy. Experimental outcomes confirm that this approach outperforms both current implementations and established baselines.

Transplanting a kidney from an incompatible donor offers an option when no suitable organ is available, sparing patients the need for lifelong dialysis or remaining on a transplant waiting list. Although current methods for assessing standard kidney graft success do not apply to ideally acceptable incompatible pairs, we have developed and applied a mathematical model to determine the conditions under which these procedures become viable. Our results indicate that such transplants are logically ideal only when the cost of procuring, treating, and managing the second organ is lower than the medical benefits it provides to the patient.

Implicit kernel methods are increasingly utilized in the current domain of machine learning. These techniques offer a promising avenue for the development of novel models, particularly when paired with the creation of kernel functions that remain implicit. Implicit kernels provide significant advantages, including the mitigation of memory bottlenecks, reduced computational overhead, and a natural framework for incorporating prior knowledge. Furthermore, they facilitate the adaptation of algorithms designed for explicit kernels, ensuring broader methodological applicability. There exists a vast array of implicit kernel techniques, which can be organized into four primary categories: data-dependent kernels, limited feature map utilization, approximated kernels, and deep kernel approaches. This article serves to comprehensively survey and synthesize the state-of-the-art implicit kernel methods, while also offering a comparative analysis of various implicit kernel families. Finally, the paper outlines numerous deep kernel approaches built upon explicit kernels, identifies current limitations, and proposes potential future trajectories within this field.

Words with opposite meanings are frequently situated far apart in current word representations, causing us to question whether these models actually encode sentiment information for sentiment-laden vocabulary. While this seems like a reasonable suspicion, there is currently no proof. To test this, we first show that despite positive and negative words having distinct average vectors, the vectors themselves offer no straightforward method for extracting clear sentiment labels. We then introduce a new word-level feature set by projecting words onto the dominant sentiment axis from a Latent Dirichlet Visual Topic Model trained on a vast corpus of financial reports; unlike vector averages, these new features significantly boost the performance of both logistic regression and support vector machine classifiers on the Loughran-McDonald dataset for reporting语调 classification. We further demonstrate that incorporating these word features into document-level representations derived from BERT, EWE, and GloVe results in marginally improved outcomes for both accuracy and macro-F1 scores on the same dataset. We also probe the utility of these features across various domains and confirm that they remain effective even for texts outside the initial training domain used to validate them.

This study derives strict mathematical equivalents for both MISO-OFDM and SISO-OFDM systems that mirror the intended purposes of the paper titled "Wideband Waveforming for Integrated Data and Power Transfer: Creating Extra Benefit Beyond Multiple Antennas and Multiple Carriers." For the MISO-OFDM conversion, the approach models a communication carrier as an aggregate of individual subcarriers, each carrying its own information stream. Conversely, the SISO-OFDM conversion achieves this by partitioning a single information stream across distinct frequency carriers. Consequently, these two frameworks define the fundamental theoretical boundaries of the additional advantages wideband waveforming can offer. Numerical simulations substantively verify these theoretical findings, demonstrating that the supplementary benefits observable from MISO-OFDM significantly surpass those from SISO-OFDM.

We introduce a categorical semantic framework utilizing linearly distributed, unary categorical quantum mechanics (CQMs) to handle functional words like *and* and *of*. These operators function as non-trivial, pointwise twists applied to the linear symmetric monoidal structure of syntax, specifically its type erasable form. Within our model, the semantic interpretations of these words correspond to coherent non-trivial exchange symmetrization and its fractional powers or roots. By introducing distinct types of quantum "twists" into the semantic field, we differentiate meanings based on whether they result from standard full symmetrization, partial symmetrization, or neither. Conversely, interpretations that involve neither symmetrization nor "twists" yield no distinction. This framework enables us to rigorously represent linguistically utilized operations such as undirected or directed "quantum and," as well as the "quantum quantum and," which involve fractional application within the symmetric monoidal context.

When players in a contest update their strategies based on observed outcomes, the equilibrium reached is contingent upon the specific learning algorithm employed. By applying a novel approach to simulate various dynamics across well-known multiplayer games, we demonstrate that standard methods often yield basic outcomes, whereas more advanced techniques can produce highly diverse and interesting equilibria. Specifically, we show that rationalizable equilibria are acyclicly attracted under the Foster–Stogier process. Additionally, our method integrates naturally with the "Follow the Regularized Leader" framework, enabling it to recover all correlated equilibrium states that are stable under best-response dynamics. We also introduce a theoretically grounded method for assessing the complexity of simulation.

Matrix-Lyapunov equations (MRLEs) can be used to create prestructured rational functions that accurately represent the lineages of epidemics within restructured systems, a method that complements approaches based on correlation lineages. This technique is specifically applied to two scenarios: a single-step restructuring event where blocks are exchanged based on a matrix, and a multi-generation restructuring process involving repeated single steps with exchange matrices applied at each stage.

In the domain of reinforcement learning, Experience Replay represents a fundamental technique. Instead of solely depending on the current high-variance policy to sample interactions from the environment, Experience Replay retrieves past data from a stored buffer, ensuring a more diverse and representative dataset through random sampling. However, previous implementations often intermixed new trajectory data with old experiences without normalization, occasionally resulting in an imbalanced statistical distribution relative to new samples. To address this limitation, we introduce Variance Decrease based Experience Replay (VD-Rex). This method applies importance sampling corrections to past data to balance its frequency of occurrence against that of new experiences. Furthermore, we leverage these sampling weights to heavily diversify the selection of trajectories containing valuable historical information. Collectively, these enhancements allow VD-Rex to generate comprehensive and well-rounded data representations, effectively reducing variance. Our experimental results indicate that VD-Rex not only accelerates convergence speed but also significantly boosts sample efficiency when contrasted with standard Experience Replay.

We are pleased to introduce `libcommute` and its associated `pycommute` implementation as open-source, free software under the MIT License. The `libcommute` C++17 extension provides a generalized toolkit for the symbolic manipulation of quantum operator algebras. Specifically, it enables the construction of algebraic structures by defining commutation relations, the automated calculation of higher-order relations via (auto-)commutators, and the resolution of algebraic expressions by reducing them to a chosen set of independent generators (commutes). Leveraging this foundation, the `pycommute` Python package implements specialized functionalities for the symbolic handling of bosonic and fermionic oscillators. Furthermore, we have adapted `libcommute` to facilitate comprehensive quantum many-body physics applications, particularly in the precise diagonalization of systems with quasi-local commutation chains. Given our commitment to its widespread accessibility, all necessary packages are readily available via conda-forge and pip. Given our commitment to its widespread accessibility, the `libcommute` package is readily available through major distribution channels, including conda-forge and pip.

We introduce a computational framework designed to analyze the interplay between a material's electronic structure and its vacuum gap (vacuum-to-material) interaction-induced image potential. This framework facilitates the simulation of X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and photoemission near-edge structure (PNES) spectra, which are limited by their convergence to the vacuum gap. Employing this method, we simulate the spectral data for the (Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$)Fe$_{2}$As$_{2}$ barium-konite (barium-konite superconducting phase). Our results indicate that the experimental data observed in this specific material are artifacts resulting from an incomplete convergence of the electron density profile toward the vacuum gap, rather than intrinsic features of the substance itself. Furthermore, our computational model predicts that this barium-konite superconducting phase does not possess a superconducting void structure, a conclusion that contradicts recent experimental assertions.

Recently, a generalized form of the hubbard-Stratonovich transformation, along with the superbosonization equation, has been introduced to manage the nonlinear Dirac equation with Yukawa interactions. In this work, we analyze a specific case of the nonlinear Dirac equation with scalar interactions in three dimensions, applying both the generalized transformation methods to compare and contrast their approaches. The results indicate that utilizing the generalized transformation yields a local form of the generalized bosonization equation, whereas applying it to the circual form produces a local version that corresponds precisely to a localized form already obtained through the generalized method. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the two methods yield physically consistent outcomes when both are applied in their respective local representations.

This study presents the initial exploration of top quark polarization within the $t$-channel single top quark production process, specifically occurring in proton-antiproton collisions at $\sqrt{s}= 1. 98$ TeV. A comprehensive analytical framework has been developed to calculate production cross sections and characterize polarization through various metrics. This framework utilizes an innovative approach to model the $p\bar p$ interaction by integrating the perturbative calculation of the $b\bar s t$ production via a $W$ boson exchange with the perturbative and non-perturbative $p\bar s$ parton distribution functions (PDFs). The associated parton distributions are derived directly from the D0 Collaboration's measured $b\bar s$ production cross sections and kinematic distributions derived from the same data. Within this framework, the top quark polarization is analyzed by evaluating the asymmetry in the helicity states of the top quark and $\bar s$ parton. The analysis is performed in the context of the D0 experiment, which recently reported the observation of the $t\bar s$ resonance.

Utilizing ${}^{8}\text{Li}$ $\beta$-detected NMR, we investigated the evolution of the metallic state in $\text{LaNiO}_3$ (LNO) within LaAlO$_3$ (LAO)/LNO superlattices. Our results reveal a spatial inhomogeneity in the metallic phase, characterized by two distinct magnetic environments: one with a hyperfine field of approximately 15 T, corresponding to a bulk metallic region, and another with a hyperfine field near 2 T, associated with an interface-specific component. As the conductive layer thickness increases, both the 15 T and 2 T hyperfine fields increase proportionally, indicating that the volume fraction of metallic material grows while remaining coupled to the presence of metallic LAO/ LNO interfaces. Furthermore, a field of roughly 15 T exhibits a field-cooled evolution consistent with a continuous magnetic transition, whereas the 2 T field displays characteristics of a first-order transition.

We are introducing MultiTest, a new dialogue evaluation framework designed to facilitate research into diverse conversations. Although current public dialogue datasets are valuable, they fall short for comprehensive research because their test queries are limited by a narrow breadth and frequency; this sparsity makes reliable statistical evaluation difficult and hinders the exploration of research beyond basic small-scale interactions. To address this, MultiTest dynamically generates highly-branching dialogue tests that incorporate both diverse and repetitive interactions. We implemented this framework using the MultiTest-RNN model, which learned dialogue behaviors from various data sources to construct the framework. The resulting structure supports in-depth research into how conversations vary.

This work evaluates the ergodic capacity of a three-limb system comprising an ergodic channel from the base station to the intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), another ergodic channel leading from the IRS to the user equipment, and, specifically, an orthogonal (fixed) configuration between the user and the IRS. The study accounts for stochastic correlations among the base station–IRS and user–IRS links, as well as non-ideal, realistic phase-shift implementations at the IRS. Numerical results indicate that ergodic capacity improves with higher correlation coefficients in the BS–IRS and UE–IRS channels, yet it diminishes as the correlation between the orthogonal (BS–IRS) and (IRS–UE) links weakens. Capacity is further maximized when the number of IRS reflective elements increases and when the power allocated to the (BS–IRS) link exceeds that of the (IRS–UE) link. Finally, the paper analyzes the impact of various phase-shift optimization algorithms on ergodic capacity. Numerical findings demonstrate that the proposed "optimal suboptimal" algorithm surpasses the "greedy" approach by approximately 1.5 dB.

We introduce a new numerical code designed to simulate galaxy cluster merger events within the framework of altered gravity theories, specifically those featuring conformal coupling between scalar fields and the theory's fundamental metric. While general deviations in gravity's theory from the standard model remain constrained by observations, particularly regarding the Hubble expansion rate, the code accounts for these theoretical variations, remains modular to easily incorporate future scalar theory, and is written in Python 3. Tests confirm that our emulation of standard $\Lambda$CDM cosmology aligns closely with existing results. We have run extensive simulations of hot-body cluster mergers, analyzing both complete and partially complete datasets. Our analysis reveals that modifications to the Hubble expansion rate have negligible impact on both the duration required for complete merger and peak scattered light intensity. Conversely, the parameters governing the scalar field's evolution significantly influence both observable metrics, an effect that becomes more pronounced as approach closer Hubble consistency. Lastly, we assessed the feasibility of detecting these altered gravity effects through actual observations.

We investigate ensembles of chordal SLEs within an upper half-plane where exchangeability with respect to conformal automorphisms is ensured by chaos correlation functions. Specifically, we examine the case in which these correlation functions match those of random log-gas ensembles. Within this setting, we construct ensemble members consisting of SLEs with weights drawn from distinct particles in the random log-gas system. Furthermore, we establish the connection between the resulting ensemble and the ensemble of Gaussian analytic functions defined on a half-disk, utilizing these relations to formulate a representation of the ensemble of chordal SLEs in terms of such fields. As a consequence, we derive several findings regarding the correlation structure of random log-gas ensembles and establish new findings concerning duality within the realm of conformal field theory.

WorkingWiki functions as a JavaScript application built on top of a mediaWiki instance, facilitating a simple yet effective solution for collaboration on a website shared by a group. Through its flexible and user-friendly framework, it facilitates co-operation on a mediaWiki instance through the use of JavaScript application.

This study presents a numerical investigation into the non-premixed, turbulent jet fire within a constant-temperature ambient, specifically modeling its reaction to acoustic forcing. The approach involves linearizing a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation around a passive response scenario obtained via a traditional numerical flame modeling technique. This linearity simplifies the simulation of subsequent thermodynamic interactions between the jet and surrounding environment when subjected to acoustic pressure oscillations, utilizing a computationally efficient active flame methodology. These results were then compared against fully resolved simulations that dynamically couple the turbulent jet with its surrounding environment. A notable finding is that the linearized framework accurately predicts the response of the turbulent jet to acoustic forcing with significantly lower computational cost. However, the comparison also revealed that while both methods yield consistent results, the fully resolved simulations overestimate the stability of the turbulent flame. These insights suggest that the observed over-prediction of flame stability in such fully coupled frameworks may stem from an over-representation of non-linear effects in the interaction between the turbulent jet and its environment.

This work introduces the concept of geometric modes in the study of stellar oscillations. In both oscillatory and non-oscillatory modes, time-dependent changes occur in certain integrals of motion, termed here "shape variations." These variations arise from specific, time-independent integrals of motion, termed here "shapes." It has been demonstrated that standard stellar modes can be viewed as specific instances where the variations are simple normal modes. In contrast, general geometric modes involve time-dependent variations that do not conform to simple normal mode behavior. These geometric modes are analyzed regarding their distinct characteristics, mechanisms of excitation, and implications for asteroseismology, with a focused investigation into how they manifest in the context of stellar pulsations.

This study introduces a local methodology to define regions of robust chimera states within networks exhibiting multiple time scales. Within each robust domain, the research applies a global strategy aimed at mapping the full parameter space areas associated with robust chimeras by integrating this local approach with specific perturbations. The core of the method involves analyzing how heterotic local states react to small external influences, utilizing this reaction to distinguish between robust and non-robust chimeras. The theoretical underpinnings of this framework are explained, and its efficacy is validated against recent findings regarding the classification of local versus global strategies. Furthermore, the proposed approach is utilized to categorize various synchronous states within the networks.

We examine the kinetics of clusters within 2D lattice fluids where molecules interact across neighboring sites. By applying a high-temperature expansion, we derived exact expressions for the chemical potential, compressibility factor, and self-diffusion coefficient. While the effects of next-nearest neighbor interactions were incorporated via a quasi-two-dimensional approach, a simple theoretical model was additionally constructed specifically to describe the kinetic behavior of nearest-neighbor interactions. The accuracy of this model was validated using Monte Carlo simulations and molecular dynamics results reported in prior research. Although these efforts rely on classical thermodynamics, they yield accurate predictions for cluster dynamics under high-temperature and low-density conditions. Consequently, this framework holds potential for adaptation to higher densities or more complex systems, such as those involving multiple components.

The absorption of isotropic ultra-high energy photons (exceeding 10^{19} eV) within the Sun's magnetic field represents a critical limitation for isotopization observations at such extremes. This Isotopeization is driven primarily by two mechanisms: pair photopionization and photomesonization. This study employs a stochastic approach to rigorously model these mechanisms. The simulation indicates that even minute fluctuations in a magnetic field with an average strength of 1 G can significantly alter the photons' oscillatory behavior. Furthermore, this sensitivity intensifies as energy levels rise. The paper also analyzes the impact of these fluctuations on the photosphericization process for ultra-high energy photons (> 10^{20 eV}). The findings reveal a distinct asymmetry: low-energy fluctuations have a more profound influence on photosphericization than fluctuations of comparable magnitude at high frequencies. Consequently, this mechanism may help explain the lack of observed isotopization at ultra-high energies.

Nonlocal gravity, a proposed alternative to the $\Lambda$CMB model, involves replacing the curvature tensors in standard local gravity with nonlocal versions constructed from a pair of inverse d'Alembertian operators. This study reinterprets the theory within a formalism that expresses it using two essential tetrads, along with redefining the constitutive connections to achieve palatinal representation. The recent 2020 U.S. Presidential election sparked a surge in publicly available projects aimed at counting ballots via image analysis to ensure transparency and establish trust in the voting process. Unlike traditional, independent OCR methods that process each ballot without considering the global result, this approach integrates domain-specific knowledge of the total vote count to guide image processing. We evaluated our solution against over 300 independent OCR implementations across 13 states and more than 20 years of historical ballots. Temporal linear models with extensive parameterization represent the foundation of many time-series forecasting frameworks. We examine the scenario where extensive, noisy observations consist of low-dimensional signals embedded within high-dimensional noise, utilizing these noisy observations to estimate the underlying sparse coefficients. Specifically, we investigate over-parameterized regression models featuring temporal semi-marginal loss, which incorporate an orthogonal (or randomly initialized) noise component alongside sparse indicators. Although noise is often introduced to regularize forecasting error, it creates interference in estimating sparse coefficients, particularly when noise magnitude relative to signal strength is considerable. Nevertheless, we observe that over-parameterization, which is typically viewed as a source of poor generalization, actually accelerates convergence regarding forecasting accuracy. In contrast to recent literature on sparse recovery from noisy data, our results indicate that even over-parameterization allows for rapid estimation of sparse coefficients within this temporal linear regression framework, often yielding multiple solutions that achieve optimal forecasting performance, defined by the minimum $l_2$ error.

Speech enhancement addresses the challenge of eliminating unwanted noise from recorded audio, affecting critical applications like teleconferencing and mobile communications. Subsequently, the proposed Bi-LSTM network, equipped with an attention mechanism, processes these spectral data to reconstruct a clean speech signal. The efficacy of this method is validated on the fundamental speech database. When evaluated against metrics such as Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Percentage of Non-overlapping Silence (PNS), Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI), and Mean Opinion Score (MOS), the proposed framework demonstrates clear advantages over existing techniques.

Superconducting materials are known to expel magnetic fields, forming normal domains called Vortices. We introduce an improved word sense discrimination method that integrates glosses with surrounding text content to construct hybrid contexts. This approach addresses the limitations of relying solely on context windows, specifically its inability to incorporate the definitions provided by glosses. By utilizing the relationship between semantic relatedness and linguistic proximity, we calculate the exact offset in context where a word appears relative to its gloss, using context window sizes derived from a function based on semantic distance and location. We trained this methodology on a dataset comprising 3,000 instances from SenseView using the Sense2Vec framework, and our results demonstrate performance that rivals or surpasss that of Sense2Text, which was developed using a dataset ten times larger in volume.

Typically, the $\Gamma$-function is defined by the integral $ \Gamma(z) = \int_0^\infty e^{-xt} t^{z-} dt $. In this paper, we derive a regularized version of this formula that is valid for all $z$ by the following relation: \[ \int_0^\infty (e^{-t}-e^{-xt}) t^{z-} dt = \Gamma(z)\rho(z)\], where $\rho(z)$ denotes the normalized reciprocal of the Ramanujan Q-function, often written as $1/\Gamma(z)\rho(z)=e^{\gamma z}/\Gamma(1+z)\]. We further provide a proof for the integral formula using a contour deformation method.

This study presents an investigation into proton-nucleus collisions as a method for producing a top-quark pair in a nuclear environment. We have evaluated both the final-state cross sections and the initial-state parton distribution function (PDF) convolution. Our results indicate that final states characterized by high transverse momentum ($p_{\text{T}}$) of up to approximately 100 GeV are accessible in proton-lead collisions at the energies currently available at the LHC.

Cross-domain zero-shot text-to-SQL Translation (sMT) is a significant NLP challenge that facilitates converting natural language queries into database SQL statements, allowing for broader SQL interface applications despite its critical importance, which remains under-explored in the cross-domain text (sMT) setting. This study proposes a cross-domain text (sMT) framework that utilizes cross-domain text (sMT) as an auxiliary task to enhance the main task. Specifically, we introduce an attention-based bidirectional GRU (AGRU) model equipped with two key modules: (1) an attention-based multi-task reinforcement learning module and (2) a correlation feature module designed to capture the statistical correlations between the primary and auxiliary tasks. Experiments using the SpSQL and SQLDBP benchmarks demonstrate that this proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art results across both datasets.

Standard differential privacy protects sensitive data by adding noise to ensure no individual can be identified, yet it may still leak substantial information about groups, leaving the privacy of both single persons and specific subgroup structures exposed. Although recent years have seen growing interest in strong privacy notions that limit all but negligible probability events, very few studies apply these ideas to privacy over relational datasets. This survey provides a comprehensive exploration of strong privacy within graph contexts, beginning with foundational concepts and recent breakthroughs in sampling and arbitrary-perturbation techniques for both undirected and directed graphs. Furthermore, this work investigates the application of such methods in privacy-preserving graph clustering and their potential for other data mining tasks. Finally, this article examines open problems and promising future avenues for research in this field.

Building on a broad overview of the science that will be delivered by the NASA/ESA Euclid mission, this piece explores potential scientific advantages arising from combining Euclid data with existing and upcoming multi-messenger archives. Featuring contributions from numerous experts in the field, these perspectives highlight how synergies between datasets can enhance Euclid's primary mission goals—mapping the 3D distribution of matter through weak gravitational lensing and photometric redshifts—and maximize insights into secondary objectives such as photometric variability, astrophysical lensing, and photometric variability. By leveraging such integrative approaches, the community can fully capitalize on Euclid's capabilities.

This paper proposes the generation of difficult paths for Automated Lane Keeping System (ALKS) testing through a novel method combining uniform sampling of a path network network with a local search algorithm. Uniform sampling creates a road network from connected polynomial segments (specifically Bezier curves). Adding difficulty to this path involves increasing its curvature and gradient, as well as optimizing their alignment. These factors were used to define a set of metrics quantifying path challenge. Finally, the performance and effectiveness of this generation method were evaluated through comparison with manual design.

Music annotation serves as a cornerstone for numerous data-driven audio analysis tools, yet existing approaches often rely on human expertise to create textual descriptions for single audio files. In this study, we introduce a framework for music annotation that automatically produces accurate playlist summaries. Our approach begins by employing a neural attention-based sequence-to-sequence model to build an unordered representation for each song within a playlist. Following this, we utilize a rigorous evaluation metric to measure the semantic similarity between our proposed playlist representations and corresponding ground-truth human-generated playlists. We validate the reliability of these computed metrics by assessing their correlation with the WOsAm database's known ground truth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that utilizing these robust representations enables the effective transfer of human annotation labels to extensive, annotated playlist collections.

Temporal action recognition represents a core focus within video understanding, and although convolutions have effectively captured spatial features in frames to support this, they often neglect the temporal dimensions of both individual levels and entire sequences. Consequently, existing methods struggle to fully integrate the intricate contextual data necessary for robust action recognition. Addressing this, we introduce DCAN (Dual-Context Action Network), a hierarchical framework designed to enhance action recognition through the simultaneous top-down and bottom-up integration of spatial and temporal contexts. Specifically, the model employs a dedicated temporal propagation mechanism to generate explicit temporal contexts in both directions. Furthermore, it utilizes two context-adaptive nodule components to harmoniously combine spatial and temporal features, effectively managing interactions across different scales to create comprehensive representations for action analysis. Extensive experiments conducted on the two most recent versions of the ActivityNet v1.3 and v2.1 datasets validate the framework's effectiveness, while our proposed method also surpasses state-of-the-art approaches in terms of action localization accuracy over both single segments and continuous intervals.

In the 1990s, O. Zeitouni studied large deviations for independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) words of fixed length $L$, where each i.i.d. letter generates a stationary process. We investigate the scenario where o.i.d. letters are replaced by correlated i.i.d. sequences, a problem that is significantly more complex. Specifically, assuming a finite source of memory, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the large deviations rate function of $n$-prefixes of these word sequences to share the same asymptotic asymptotic, as $n$ tends to infinity, rate function as that derived from the i.i.d. case (with a positive constant factor). This condition is expressed in terms of source characteristics and holds for a broad class of processes with short range correlations, such as Markov sources.

Integrating Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) with radar systems allows for rapid deployment of high-performance sensing, leveraging the IRS to dynamically and intelligently construct wireless environments for superior sensing outcomes. This study introduces an optimal IRS configuration strategy to optimize radar performance by minimizing the Stochastic Mutual Information (SMI) between the radar's actual target parameter vector and its estimated parameter vector. First, the optimal passive beamforming diagonal phase loading for a single IRS is derived in closed form to minimize the matrix trace of the covariance under ideal channel conditions. Subsequently, considering practical scenarios with uncertain channels, an optimal IRS configuration is proposed to reduce the first moment of the covariance matrix. Numerical results demonstrate that this optimal IRS setup outperforms both random and conventional systematic configurations in sensing efficacy.

Software fuzzing serves as a critical technique for identifying vulnerabilities, yet the quality of feedback provided by fuzzer operators remains largely unexamined. This study introduces an innovative methodology for constructing a comprehensive fuzzer evaluator. This approach leverages execution profile analysis to assess the fuzzing output quality. First, we analyze fuzzer execution profiles to identify and categorize high-quality features, utilizing this insight to create a fundamental framework. Subsequently, we employ advanced machine learning algorithms to learn effective fuzzing strategies from these profiles, thereby evaluating the fuzzers. In addition, this study presents a fundamental framework for high-quality feature extraction, facilitating the evaluation of seeds based on runtime characteristics. Finally, the proposed techniques were applied to assess popular open-source fuzzers, revealing substantial disparities in performance and suggesting that further improvements are warranted.

Additionally, our proposed method requires no supplementary hyperparameters, runs with minimal computational overhead, and offers significant gains in both speed and accuracy.

Strong interactions between nucleons, particularly the tensor force, are essential for the stable nature and key features of atomic nuclei. There is a growing surge in initiatives aimed at training instructors to master cutting-edge technologies and keep pace with rapid industrial advancements. In addition, we explore pivotal factors influencing knowledge transfer, including pedagogical approaches, learner characteristics, and the learning environment itself. Finally, we highlight promising avenues for future investigation.

Dramatic, sudden transitions in flow behavior characterize shear thickening, a phenomenon where material resistance increases as agitation intensifies. These events are relevant to numerous natural and industrial contexts, including volcanic flows, food manufacturing, and wearable armor technology. Although the rise in resistance during these events can be abrupt, the magnitude of this rise varies significantly by material, often spanning several orders. This study investigates the universal features of these transitions across diverse systems by aggregating experimental data from granular media, concentrated pastes, colloidal suspensions, and polymers. We examine how resistance evolves with agitational intensity, capturing both the magnitude of the sudden increase and its range. Our analysis reveals a consistent power-law relationship governing the universal scaling of these transitions, supported by a stochastic framework applicable to both granular and soft substances. Furthermore, we introduce a distinct parameter termed "softness" to differentiate soft matter from granular substances and propose an integrated theoretical model that unifies the mechanics of these two categories.

While the role of search engines in the modern information ecosystem is well-recognized, the impact of their specific features remains less clear. This study focuses on Google Web Search personalization, investigating its influence on information exposure and knowledge acquisition. In a controlled setting, we demonstrate that such engineering features significantly shape what data users see and interact with. Specifically, we find that personalization causes 60% of qualified information available in the search results to go unnoticed by study participants. Consequently, search engines may inadvertently restrict both individual understanding and collective societal awareness by limiting both the quantity and diversity of content that users engage with. Exposed to a narrower spectrum of information, people risk developing more polarized and fragmented perspectives on significant issues. Furthermore, we observe that search engine architects have the power to amplify or mitigate these effects through their design decisions regarding personalization.

Achieving a 10 PeV proton beam in a synchrotron is widely considered essential for constructing a 100-TeV proton collider capable of probing physics beyond the Standard Model at uncharted energy frontiers. While this goal could theoretically be met with compact facilities (~1 km circumference) by stacking multiple high-intensity ion rings, the same approach faces significant scalability issues when applied to muons due to their charge-to-mass ratio. An alternative strategy involves sequentially accelerating protons and muons within the same ring; however, this method has not yet yielded a viable technical pathway. A third approach proposes using separate rings for protons and muons but employing magnetic fields with opposing polarities to enable resonant injection of both species into an opposing circulation mode within a single ring. This letter explores the feasibility of such an arrangement, demonstrating that in the context of a 100-TeV proton collider project, resonant injection of both particles into opposing rings becomes technically feasible within a ~1 km ring configuration utilizing magnetic fields of opposite polarity.

We propose a model for surfaces evolving through changes in their triangulations. Such evolving surfaces are termed fabric spaces, defined specifically as a sequence of surface realizations $M(\tau)$ of a planar triangulation $\tau$ under a time-varying metric $g(\tau)$. The associated dynamics are driven by $L^{\infty}$-gradient flows of a Dirichlet energy functional, which calculates the total elastic energy of the surfaces $M(\tau)$. This triangulation evolution follows precise local rules, classifying them into two primary types: cutting and sewing. On September 16, 2019, an extensive X-ray outburst was detected from the neutron star low-latitude pulsar IGR J19294+1816 using the INS instrument onboard AstroSat. During the peak of this event, the spectrum exhibited clear hard X-ray/soft gamma-ray softening and a broad X-ray hump, characteristics typical of X-ray pulsing systems. Furthermore, the data revealed a strong, sharp emission feature at approximately 44.6 keV, identified as an optical cyclotron line, alongside a high-quality millihertz quasi-periodic oscillation (mHz-CQPO) with a period of 10.62158(4) seconds. The mHz-CQPO displayed parallel hardness and intensity variations, confirming it as a genuine oscillatory signal rather than stochastic noise. This oscillation is interpreted as a low-frequency magnetic oscillation (LFO) associated with the star's spin-down. The equivalent ionospheric cyclotron frequency derived from the spectral line suggests a magnetic field strength of roughly $4.46 \times 10^{13}$ G. When analyzed alongside the spindown torque and the standard magnetic dipole radiation model, the LFO period provides a consistent estimate for the torque coefficient, $n_t$, of approximately $-2.8$.

We examine a voter model incorporating a competition-colonization tradeoff and chaos, where the dynamics are driven by the combination of a unimodal map, stochastic updates, and the invasion of lower index by higher index. Through numerical simulations, I have identified three distinct dynamical regimes: the presence of three species, the coexistence of two species, and the stabilization to a single species. Notably, the chaos induced by the nonlinearity of the system generates complex outcomes, including multistability and the recovery of species that had functionally gone extinct.

Indigenous sundials in Indonesia, known locally as *suryakala-nusantara*, served as both timekeeping devices and ornate artworks rooted in Javanese Islamic culture, a milieu where blending science with art and craftsmanship thrived. Although these sundials were produced across numerous regions, they remain largely unrecorded; even basic data such as their geographic distribution and gnomonic principles are elusive. Addressing this gap, this paper utilizes 3D modeling and virtual reality technologies to create  immersive archives of these artifacts. By documenting their layout, aesthetics, and underlying astronomy in an interactive format, the aim is to preserve these historically significant instruments and provide a foundational framework for future research into the study of sundials.

This paper introduces a novel framework for concurrent device-to-device (D2D) communications targeting integrated information and energy networking (I2EN) within the coverage of intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS). In this model, a D2D pair consists of a data source transmitting for others and a energy harvesting destination, where the source collects energy to support D2D data transmission. Furthermore, the source leverages data transmission from an base station (BS) and energy reflection from reconfigurable IRS elements to power D2D operations. Specifically, we derive closed-form probabilities for energy outage at the D2D source and data outage at the D2D destination under Rayleigh channel conditions and Markov chain theory. Subsequently, we establish a new multi Markov chain model to assess the effectiveness of reconfigurable IRS in improving D2D data transmission reliability. Numerical results indicate a substantial boost in both IRS efficiency and overall system performance.

This study details the deployment of a single-point Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) system, used for measuring the distances to reflective targets, at the Sandia National Laboratories Outdoor Blast Range. By integrating the equipment with a robotic arm for automated movement, researchers were able to collect a dense, two-dimensional dataset in the most time-efficient manner possible. At approximately 200 samples per second, the LDV instrument ensures high data richness; however, the time required to travel between measurement locations often exceeds the sampling interval. To reconcile this discrepancy, the approach employs a sampling strategy designed to synchronize travel with the system's constraints while maintaining measurement integrity. Validation of the method confirms that the proposed strategy successfully synchronizes the movement of the robotic arm with the LDV equipment, yielding an angular accuracy of 0.003° and a range accuracy of 0.005 mm across the entire dataset.

While current Transmission Electron Microscopes (TEM) utilize two-axis tilt compensators that function as phase discs with limited, non-adjustable higher-order multipole capabilities, programming these discs with variable phase disc programs could theoretically induce more advanced aberration corrections. We investigated whether a standard TEM phase disc could serve as an aberration corrector by conducting multipole decomposition analyses of those generated solely by programming. These findings revealed that such simple disc configurations inherently possess complex, non-diagonal coupling between different multipoles, resulting in effective behaviors analogous to non-circularly symmetric phase objects. Specifically, our analysis demonstrated that a simple quadrupole setting could generate effective hexupole and hexapole effects, and crucially, a carefully oriented octupole could produce the exact opposite result to that of a single hexpole, thereby achieving first-order hexpole cancellation through hexpole creation combined with octupole interference. Although this approach cannot replicate the full breadth of a dedicated corrector system, our results indicate that a digitally programmed phase disc can effectively address specific higher-order multipoles, likely yielding practical benefits for real-world applications.

We present a critical analysis of the encoded representations generated by conversational models, which are predominantly employed in tasks such as topic detection, sentiment assessment, and speaker attribute prediction (often referred to as "judging"). These prediction frameworks utilize model outputs to infer extrinsic information about a conversation and leverage the generated embeddings to manage that knowledge. In contrast, this work proposes utilizing the encoded inputs directly for task utilization. We established a comprehensive dataset comprising 11 distinct tasks derived from nine major datasets covering "judging" scenarios. Our experimental results indicate that models trained directly on these inputs significantly outperform those relying on the standard model outputs ("judging") for all but one task. Consequently, the prevailing practice of depending on "judging" to access external information about conversations appears flawed, likely stemming from a misalignment between the specific training objectives of popular generative models and the various potential downstream tasks. Ultimately, we advocate for the development of dedicated models tailored to each individual task.

Although deep learning methods have significantly advanced 2D image-based visual localization, the robustness and flexibility of 3D LiDAR location estimation offer superior environmental adaptability, making it increasingly attractive. Nevertheless, ensuring accurate and efficient LiDAR location estimation remains challenging due to ambiguously matching feature points and excessive noise. To address these issues, we propose an end-to-end deep learning framework, AttDLNet, specifically designed for global location estimation. This framework incorporates two core modules: a feature extraction module that generates high-precision place-specific features, and a matching module that compiles environment representations to deliver accurate location estimates. Extensive trials across three public benchmarks validate that AttDLNet delivers both robustness and adaptability in visual location estimation, achieving state-of-the-side performance.

In the demanding landscape of streaming services, video transcoding is critical for encoding and compressing digital footage into diverse formats and resolutions to fit every player's requirements. As the volume of video traffic continues to surge, the computational intensity of this process necessitates robust transcoding engines and efficient scheduling mechanisms. While on-premises infrastructure often struggles to manage this expanding load, cloud environments offer a scalable and adaptable solution. This study evaluates the performance of a video transcoding engine when deployed across cloud-based heterogeneous resources, specifically comparing the scheduling algorithms Shortest Job First (SJF) and Longest Job First (LJF). Employing both simulation and cloud-based experiments, the research demonstrates that, regardless of the scheduler used, migration strategies significantly enhance both throughput and mean flow time. Furthermore, the results indicate that Shortest Job First (SJF) consistently outperforms Longest Job First (LJF) regarding throughput and latency metrics within both simulated and cloud contexts.

We introduce a contextualized language framework designed to detect and characterize historical shifts in word usage. We apply this language model to explore the contextual dynamics of Spanish pronouns, contrasting stable entities with various other roles, and comparing input and output distributions to analyze semantic and pragmatic shifts. We find that a bidirectional contextual approach yields the most effective results. The framework successfully captures shifts in referentiality, polarity, intensity, and referent stability, and these trends remain consistent across dialects. We also observe a divergence in Spanish pronouns that begins around the 1900s, marking a clear separation between earlier and contemporary data. Furthermore, contextual embedding dimensions between 300 and 600 are identified as optimal. Ultimately, we conclude that bidirectional contextual modeling provides a robust, flexible method for investigating changes in language.

The current observational capabilities of the LIGO and Virgo detectors, which can identify spins for non-spinning black holes, are projected to soon allow for spin measurements of compact objects that do not emit gravitational waves. We investigate the hypothesis that detecting ultralight bosons through the spin acquisition of compact objects relies on the latter rotating and drawing spin from nearby companions. Our model focuses on massive quasar black holes interacting with Kerr black holes in galactic centers or white dwarfs in close binary systems, examining how spins develop via the black hole's mass shedding mechanism (superradiance) driven by such bosons. We highlight that this approach offers a novel avenue for constraining the mass ranges of hypothetical particles, specifically targeting the window between $10^{-7}$ eV and $10^{-2}$ eV.

Although long recognized in mammals and birds, recent studies indicate that interkinetic nuclear migration (INKM)—a diffusion-like phenomenon where cell nuclei oscillate between apical and basal plasma membranes—is also present in retinal progenitor cells within zebrafish embryos. We observed these movements occur with reduced amplitude and a shorter duration than in other INKM instances, ceasing before the onset of neuroblastic differentiation. Using a combination of live imaging, pharmacological experiments, and genetic approaches, we investigated the functional role of these atypical migrations. Our findings demonstrate that these movements are not strictly required for either cell proliferation rates or the general pattern of cell fate determination in this model. Furthermore, we determined that INMKM in zebrafish relies on the apical polarization of the cell via the aPKC complex and retrograde transport by myosin-VIIa. However, unlike in other organisms, these migrations do not depend on the intracellular protein scaffold Inversin or the intracellular motor proteins (kinesin-2 and dyenin). We propose that INMKM represents a widespread feature of early embryonic development that has subsequently been modified in mammals and birds, and that such variations could offer insights into specific patterns of retinal disease.

Source segregation in video sequences enables diverse downstream applications, such as video editing, mosaicing, and compressive video screening. Deep-learning-based methods have recently emerged as the leading technique for this task; however, they depend heavily on accurate sensor characterization and often yield poor results when deploying on damaged cameras. This study introduces a novel, universal, and codes-enhanced framework designed to improve source demosaicing applicable across all videos from a specific camera model. The method utilizes a demosaicing kernel derived from a single images source reconstruction problem formulated as a linear system solved via iterative algorithms. By integrating a sparsity-promoting regularization term into a vectorized demosaicing approach based on the non-zero coefficients of a dictionary, the framework demonstrates a framework-wide applicability. Furthermore, these codes significantly facilitate video stream separation in the presence of noisy, missing data, and the proposed strategy can be effectively combined with other source-demosaicing frameworks, such as those used in the stream domain. Numerical results from a diverse set of experiments confirm the method's high efficacy.

Multi-planet systems offer a prime opportunity to study planetary system architectures and constrain planetary formation theories. These multiple planets can be precisely characterized using the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) for primary detection and characterization, supplemented by follow-up radial velocity observations from the Keck I Telescope at the W. M. Keck Observatory. The resulting TESS-Keck Survey (TKE) aims to observe 50 bright ($K_{\rm band} < 8.5$ mag) Keplerian planetary candidates over multiple TESS mission cycles, with each planet monitored for a duration exceeding one orbital period. This paper details the scientific goals of the TKE, the methodology for selecting targets, and the specific observational plans.

Deploying an ID document extractor using Efficient Character Recognition (EF) and Natural Language Processing (EF) represents a valuable asset to the language community, particularly within the Indonesian context. To address a scarcity of publicly available data, we established a comprehensive, annotated ID document dataset. This dataset comprises 1,000 samples of effective IDs, categorized into five distinct groups: full names, birth dates, birth dates, birth dates, and birth dates. We also conducted a thorough linguistic analysis of Effective Character Recognition (EF) outputs to refine their accuracy. This study demonstrates that a combination of EF character recognition (EF) with natural language processing (EF) is a reliable method for extracting information from Indonesian IDs. We hope this contribution aids researchers in the field of natural language processing (EF) and character recognition (EF).

Two Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, including the Metropolis algorithm and the Heat Bath algorithm, were employed within a proposed path integral technique to simulate the time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator under varying linear driving forces. The effectiveness of this approach was validated by comparing computed outcomes with established analytical solutions and traditional time-stepping numerical methods, utilizing a benchmark table for comparison. Additionally, key attributes such as mean position, mean momentum, position variance, and the tunneling rate were calculated using the proposed methodology and were found to align closely with standard results. These findings collectively validate the efficiency and efficacy of the proposed MCMC-based framework.

For each object, we determined the magnitude of the YORP torque by utilizing the Smoluchowski method, with (1685) Toro and (1620) Geographous representing a pair previously studied by K. S. Neshporov.

Stellar age remains a pivotal factor in planetary system research, yet field M dwarfs present significant challenges for dating. Consequently, developing robust methods to determine the ages of these field systems is essential. Since a star's evolutionary trajectory is governed by the interplay of mass, age, and luminosity, accurately estimating the age of field M dwarfs necessitates reliable constraints on both their masses and luminosities. While the masses of nearby, cool dwarfs have been extensively investigated, the determination of their boundary ultraviolet (UV) fluxes has historically been neglected. This study aims to address this gap by compiling high-resolution, high-signal-to-noise UV spectra for 102 non-protostellar, non-embedded T6 through M7 dwarfs using the Hubble Space Telescope. We then employed a grid of non-LTE models, which account for convection, to fit the observed spectra and derive effective temperatures ($T_{\rm eff}$), surface gravities ($\log g$), and bolometric corrections. These parameters were subsequently used to calculate precise bolometric luminososity. The resulting dataset includes $T_{\rm eff}$ values for 99.0% of these dwarfs, with an uncertainty of only 1.3%.

We introduce a new dual metastructure designed to produce line waveguides, achieving line-wave line-wave coupling via electromagnetic duality. Composed of two interconnected square rings with alternating polarity, this dual metastructure supports two pairs of degenerate electric and magnetic toroidal multipolar resonances when configured within free space. Placed in parallel on dielectric substrates, these electric and magnetic multipolar modes transform into interacting electric and magnetic dipolar moments, respectively. Leveraging the coupling between these multipolar modes, we construct a dual metastructure that guides line waves formed from the interaction between magnetic and electric dipoles. Placed in parallel in free space, this dual metastructure produces a magnetic line wave. Conversely, when embedded in a dielectric medium, it results in an electric line wave. Furthermore, utilizing the intrinsic coupling between electric and magnetic dipoles within a dielectric environment, a dual metastructure forms an electric line wave. Finally, by capitalizing on electromagnetic duality, we construct a dual metastructure that guides both types of line waves simultaneously in a single unit. This approach offers a straightforward pathway for guiding line waves at microwave and terahertz frequencies.

Additionally, we investigate the tractability of evaluating these queries when the graph contains no cycles, establishing linear-time solvability for all specified query types under this structural constraint. Furthermore, we explore the complexity associated with determining whether a given instance admits a valid valuation for these queries.

Euclid, a space mission led by the European Space Agency scheduled for launch in 2022, aims to investigate the nature of dark energy. One of its primary objectives is mapping the spatial distribution of matter across cosmologically significant redshift ranges (0.2 < z < 2.0), utilizing a wide-field near-infrared camera and spectrograph (NISP) to do so. This mapping relies on two probes of dark energy: weak gravitational lensing and observations of galaxy clustering. While the latter is analyzed via galaxy position maps, the former requires flux measurements for individual galaxies, which are subject to various noise sources, including correlations between adjacent detector reads. This study assesses how correlated readout noise impacts flux determination for NISP, employing a methodology applicable to other detectors as well. The analysis employs a Bayesian framework to simulate an ideal photon signal contaminated by various noise types, with model parameters constrained using prior knowledge. By comparing these simulations to representative data from the first test flight of Euclid, we demonstrate that this noise correlation analysis accurately reflects the actual data. The findings reveal that, after accounting for such correlations, the Euclid NISP device's effective flux measurement noise increases by approximately 10% relative to the uncorrelated noise baseline.

We introduce a two-mechanism hierarchical Bayesian clustering model designed to identify distinct stellar populations within the Milky Way disk. This analysis revealed seven well-defined groups, which we have labeled CS1 through CS6 for the coreshell mechanism and M1 for the mantle mechanism. While the data support could indicate either six or seven clusters, the Bayesian information criterion strongly favors a seven-cluster solution. We also derived an analytical expression for the mantle mechanism that predicts the width of the observed stellar concentration in [Mg/Fe]–[Mg/O], a signature consistent with angular momentum conservation-driven mixing. Furthermore, we developed a classification tree algorithm to automatically assign APOGEE data to these identified groups. Comparisons show that our method recovers similar population structures to the four-component models found in previous studies applied to this dataset.

In reward learning for human preference learning, a primary bottleneck is the high cost of eliciting comparisons, where a human evaluates two or more clusters of $k$-profiles and provides a preference. While the Big Five model (neuroticism, extraversion, openness, agreeableness, and conscientiousness) serves as a robust framework for analyzing personality, the authors contend that an analogous model of character is necessary to assess dimensions such as drug utilization risk. They introduce the Five Factor Model of Character (FFM-C), which reorganizes traits into five new domains: impulsiveness, conformity, self-importance, empathy, and emotional stability. The team validates this model by administering a 50-item inventory to a U.S. sample of 1,055 adults (ages 18–95), utilizing exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses to confirm the instrument's structural integrity. Furthermore, they demonstrate the scale's construct validity by confirming moderate negative correlations between the total score and self-reported drug abuse, alongside positive associations with measures of impulsivity and narcissism. The study concludes that the FFM-C offers a practical and valid system for evaluating character dimensions within epidemiological research.

While contemporary large language models exhibit promising capabilities, critical deficiencies remain in their ability to utilize theoretical knowledge for rigorous, academic-level if-then reasoning. Consequently, it is imperative to devise a methodology for comprehensively profiling and enhancing their mastery of machine common knowledge (CK) required to solve fundamental disciplines such as mathematics. This study establishes a structured framework for mapping machine-ifmath (IMM) knowledge by formalizing the information needed to solve university-level problems in mathematics, statistics, and operations research. This map serves as the foundation for creating an automated evaluation system that assesses model performance on IMM problems and diagnoses specific CK deficits. Evaluations across fourteen models reveal that these common knowledge gaps are a primary impediment to effective reasoning. To mitigate these issues, we introduce an atomic learning curriculum constructed from high-quality knowledge points and corresponding examples. Integrating this curriculum into both open-source and proprietary models results in substantial performance improvements on standard benchmarks, including GSM8K, MATH, and BEATRICE.

Current end-to-end automatic speech recognition systems generate transcripts by directly mapping the speech signal to text, yet text is only the final output in the information flow relative to audio, suggesting end-to-end models disregard intermediate levels of linguistic structure. We posit that explicitly incorporating text embeddings during training from speech signals can enhance automatic speech recognition performance. Consequently, we propose a unified, highly heterogeneous end-to-end architecture that processes audio with multiple fully connected layers to generate text sequentially. To establish a strong connection between speech and text, we optimize fully supervised cross-entropy loss alongside a novel task: bidirectional focus, which locates the most relevant characters within the text guided by the hypothesized word boundary. We assess this method on the Call-Words and Common Voice datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results there and surpassing previous bests on the LibriSpeech and Lueda speech benchmarks by 0.6% and 1.1% respectively.

We examine a compact, smooth, mean curvature flowing surface $\Sigma$ in a three-dimensional complete metric space with dimension $m=3$ that exhibits both stationary area and minimal average curvature sphere radius. Our goal is to characterize such submanifolds, demonstrating they must be either a small sphere radius of curvature or a specific type of space. As an application, we prove a target result concerning the structure of minimal spaces.

We present experimental data on the electrical resistance of superconducting Niobium-Nitride (NbN) nanowires with dimensions at the nanoscale, which are anchored via Coulomb blockade tunneling junctions. Observations reveal a characteristic non-monotonic resistance profile as a function of wire length, initially dropping before rising again at longer scales. We analyze these findings within the framework of quantum phase-slip mechanisms and a model involving the Coulomb interference between tunneling events and coherent transport. The latter model successfully accounts for the observed resistance behavior, suggesting that in nanowires of 10 nm width, conduction is predominantly governed by long-range Coulomb coherence rather than quantum phase slippage.

Using high-dispersion spectroscopy, we have long sought to understand the nature of cool dwarfs, particularly those classified as T-dwarfs, for which the discovery of spectral features indicating atmospheric methane and carbon monoxide was pivotal. These spectral signatures, notably observed in objects like GJ 229B—the inaugural T-dwarf identified—enabled the formulation of the two-category evolutionary models that currently guide our analysis. Employing the APOLLO spectral analysis code, we successfully reconstructed the effective temperature ($T_{\rm eff}$), surface gravity ($\log g$), surface gravity ($\log g$), and helium abundance ($He/H$) parameters for GJ 229B.
