Local magnetic field anomalies often interfere with sensitive atomic clock and magnetometer measurements. This study details the implementation of an atomic interferometer capable of recording oscillating local magnetic field fluctuations within a niobium superconducting cavity that exhibits a strong Meissner effect. By leveraging the strong magnetic field shielding provided by the superconducting cavity and combining it with magnetic field gradients applied via coils, we created periodic oscillations of the interferometer's atomic path. These oscillations generated distinct interference patterns, allowing for the clear observation of residual magnetic field impacts on atom density. Analysis of these effects enabled the sensitive quantification of local field alterations, with a measured magnetic field sensitivity of 0.1 fT/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$.

The magnetocaloric effect (MCE) is a phenomenon where a magnetic material undergoes a temperature change upon exposure to or removal of an external magnetic field. Although widely recognized as a cornerstone of green, energy-efficient technologies, the fundamental mechanisms driving the massive MCE observed in certain materials—specifically its enormous magnitude in room-temperature magnetic insulators like EuO and EuS, which far exceeds that of similar metals—remain unclear. Addressing this mystery, this study demonstrates that massive MCE in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) is triggered by the combined action of broken inversion symmetry and the emergence of spontaneous spin splitting. Furthermore, we elucidate, through k-space analysis, how these components promote massive MCE by enhancing both the material's magnetic sensitivity and its thermodynamic stability fluctuations.

Nanometer-scale metallic structures often exhibit nonlocal electron behavior and a spill-over effect at their boundaries, phenomena that significantly affect their optical characteristics. To analyze how these factors influence gap-plasmons under ultra-thin metal films separated by dielectric gaps, we developed a bi-nonlocal model incorporating boundary conditions. Our analysis reveals that spill-over effect and nonlocality modify electromagnetic field distributions and dispersion curves in distinct ways: field confinement at the film surfaces is driven by nonlocality, whereas the maximum field intensity within the gap is enhanced by the spill-over effect. Furthermore, at frequencies where light cannot propagate in a single film (above the single-film plasmon frequency), nonlocality induces strong dispersion, shifting the plasmon frequency lower, while the spill-over effect has minimal impact in this context. Our findings demonstrate that at spacings below 10 nm, nonlocality and spill-over effect substantially alter both field distribution patterns and light-matter interactions, particularly near or beyond the plasmon break-down frequency, making them essential considerations in both experimental analysis and theoretical modeling.

Substantive progress has been made in creating substitution variants for term rewriting systems (TRS) within the lambda calculus, yet rewriting rules targeting $\beta$-normal forms (BNF) within the Calculus of Constructions (CoC) remain largely uncharted territory. This paper presents the first exploration into this domain. We introduce a normalization procedure tailored for CoC that operates on terms containing rewriting rules. The process begins by introducing a subclass of CoC known as CoC$_0$, defined by the constraint that all terms must be in pre-COC form. We demonstrate that every term can be transformed into CoC$_0$ while simultaneously preserving its type, a property established through rewriting. Furthermore, we show that the rewrite system restricted to CoC$_0$ is both monoterm and confluent when applied to terms and their corresponding types.

To help us understand the core ideas of anomalous localized conductivities and Berry phase, we have investigated a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. By conducting an in-depth analysis of this system, we discovered that anomalous patterns of electron termination are linked to the breaking time symmetry within the lattice. We also learned that while these physical phenomena and geometric phase concepts are connected, a direct equivalence between them is not always present. Furthermore, our study highlights the practical potential of the SSH framework for realizing the anomalous Hall Hall effect using a one-dimensional electron system.

We utilize a blend of probabilistic geometry and Choquet theory to derive a fresh, intuitive representation for finite parametric mixtures. This new formulation positions mixtures as an integral composite of their constituent components. By employing this integral formulation, we also provide an illustrative visualization of parameter overfitting in finite parametric mixtures.

We examine dual-loop supergravity theories on AdS5×S5 within the framework of N=4 super Yang-Mills conformal field theory. By leveraging the observation that multi-loop amplitudes in flat space can be reconstructed from their flat-space limits, we construct these bulk integrals directly from flat-space data. Our findings indicate that when considered as functions of both bulk and external kinematic variables, multi-loop supergravity integrations exhibit distinct behaviors. Specifically, they decompose into two categories: dual-loop supergravity integrals, which contain a standard loop integral alongside an additional "dual" integral, and local terms. Crucially, we observe that this newly defined dual integral is free of infrared divergences when evaluated in flat space, whereas the conventional loop integrals retain such divergences.

Object-oriented programming is the predominant paradigm for GPU computing due to its capacity for code reuse and abstraction. However, existing GPU object allocators typically employ a single-threaded, dynamic approach that creates significant bottlenecks, necessitating the development of multi-threaded architectures to enhance performance. This study analyzes the memory access patterns of multithreaded GPU allocators to introduce DynaSOAr, a new framework combining discrete addresses with a size-ordered bitmapped free-list management system. Unlike current solutions, DynaSOAr integrates multiple distinct per-thread heaps to mitigate access conflicts across different data granularity levels. Furthermore, it utilizes discrete addresses to guarantee deterministic, collision-free memory accesses. Evaluation results demonstrate that DynaSOAr surpasses the efficacy of prior methods in terms of per-iteration performance and iteration count.

This paper investigates the boundedness properties of a class of sublinear operators denoted by $S_\sigma$ (where $0 < \sigma \le 1$) and their commutators within the framework of generalized mixed Morrey spaces and generalized Morrey-Lio ison spaces $\text{(I+I)}$. Furthermore, a model incorporating the correlation length of droplets accurately accounts for this unique dependence on textural arrangement.
